descriptor: Ideas, culture and food writing in print style

voice.summary: The Quarterly Post sounds like a good feature desk: vivid, specific headlines and deck lines with a dry aside. It prefers a fisherman and a patient cat to a trend.
dos: Write headlines as small scenes with a place and a person
Keep deck lines to one sentence with one surprising detail
Label sections plainly: Ideas, Culture, Food
donts: No clickbait numbers or 'you will not believe'
Avoid vague superlatives like amazing or epic

taglines: The long way to the news
Stories worth missing the last ferry for
Ideas, culture and a decent crossing
boilerplate: The Quarterly Post is an editorial magazine of essays, reportage and food writing, published as a front page with a featured story and a Most Read column.
